args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN OF REORGANIZATION — DEVIATION REPORT
Committee Redline vs. Debtor’s Original Plan
Matter: Bankruptcy Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization
Output: plan-deviation-report.docx
Status: For internal counsel use

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This report compares the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors’ redlined Plan of Reorganization (the “Committee Redline”) against the Debtor’s original filed Plan of Reorganization (the “Debtor Plan”), reconciled against (i) the attached valuation summary, (ii) the deal-team transmittal / partner email thread, and (iii) the disclosure statement excerpts and related schedules/exhibits.

Three material deviations introduced by the Committee Redline require decision:

1. Indemnification / recovery architecture — indemnification cap silently reduced; claims basket converted from deductible to tipping basket.
2. Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already disclosed and at issue in this case.
3. Survival / limitation period — shortened survival for core representations, conflicting with the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email — supersedes earlier thread messages): the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping), but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. Indemnification-cap and MAE carve-out positions remain open for negotiation but are not designated walk-away on the current record.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. SOURCE MATERIALS REVIEWED
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Debtor Plan (base / firm-standard plan architecture)
B. Committee Redline (counterparty markup of the Plan)
C. Valuation summary (enterprise and recovery support underlying plan economics)
D. Transmittal email / deal-team correspondence (partner thread; latest message controls)
E. Disclosure statement excerpts and schedules/exhibits:
   • Schedule 3.7 — pending regulatory inquiries
   • Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities
   • Exhibit B — survival matrix
F. Engagement instruction requiring a plan-deviation report grounded in the foregoing

Note: Disclosure schedules control over general statements in the base materials. Each scheduled exception that intersects a markup change is called out below.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. DEVIATION MATRIX
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP (Silent Reduction)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Plan topic:           Plan treatment / estate and post-emergence indemnification and related recovery mechanics supporting plan distributions and residual estate obligations
Debtor Plan:          Firm-standard indemnification cap retained at negotiated baseline level supporting disclosed recoveries
Committee Redline:    Cap silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out in redline summary narrative)
Intersection with
schedules/valuation:  Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the reduced cap would silently shift away from the indemnifying parties and onto the reorganized estate / residual stakeholders; valuation summary recovery waterfalls assume baseline cap support for those liabilities
Economic / plan
effect:               Downward pressure on effective recoveries for classes relying on indemnity-backed residual value; potential re-open of feasibility and best-interests analysis if cap cut is material relative to Schedule 5.2 exposure
Client posture
(controlling email):  Not designated walk-away; open to negotiate. Do not treat as conceded.
Recommendation:       REJECT silent reduction. Require express markup, quantum disclosure in the disclosure statement, and conforming revision to valuation recovery exhibit. Counter: restore baseline cap, or accept limited step-down only if Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are carved out of the reduced-cap regime and separately reserved.

DEVIATION 2 — BASKET STRUCTURE (Deductible → Tipping)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Plan topic:           Indemnity / claim basket governing when plan-related indemnity or true-up claims begin to pay
Debtor Plan:          Deductible basket (claims pay only above the basket; basket amount is absorbed)
Committee Redline:    Converts basket to tipping basket (once threshold met, claims pay from dollar one)
Intersection with
schedules/valuation:  Interacts with Schedule 5.2 retained-liability inventory and with valuation-summary sensitivity on contingent claim leakage; tipping structure increases expected indemnity outflow versus deductible
Economic / plan
effect:               Moderately creditor-/claimant-favorable relative to Debtor Plan; incremental cost should be modeled in valuation update but is within the band the client has authorized to concede
Client posture
(controlling email):  CONCEDE. Latest partner instruction expressly authorizes concession of the basket conversion. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority are superseded and must not be followed.
Recommendation:       ACCEPT tipping-basket conversion. Document concession in the issues list and confirm conforming disclosure-statement language so voting parties see the economic shift. No further hold on this point.

DEVIATION 3 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Plan topic:           MAE / condition and covenant architecture affecting plan consummation conditions, termination rights, and related disclosure
Debtor Plan:          Standard MAE definition without special carve-out for the regulatory actions at issue
Committee Redline:    Adds carve-outs for regulatory action “of exactly the kind at issue in this matter,” narrowing what can constitute an MAE
Intersection with
schedules/valuation:  Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that directly intersect the new carve-outs. The scheduled exceptions control over general MAE language. Valuation summary does not presently haircut consummation risk for an MAE walk based on those inquiries if carved out.
Economic / plan
effect:               Shifts consummation and termination risk away from the party that would invoke MAE based on the Schedule 3.7 inquiries; may impair leverage if regulatory path deteriorates between confirmation and effective date
Client posture
(controlling email):  Not designated walk-away; open issue. Must be reconciled expressly against Schedule 3.7.
Recommendation:       REJECT blanket regulatory carve-out as drafted. Counter: (a) limit carve-out to ordinary-course examinations that do not result in material fine, injunction, or license impairment; (b) expressly preserve MAE treatment for adverse resolutions of the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries; and (c) require updated disclosure-statement risk factors and, if needed, a valuation sensitivity for regulatory downside.

DEVIATION 4 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Plan topic:           Survival matrix for plan-related representations, release effectiveness conditions, and post-effective-date claim assertion windows
Debtor Plan / 
Exhibit B:            Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for core representations (baseline periods control)
Committee Redline:    New limitation period shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B
Intersection with
schedules/valuation:  Exhibit B is the controlling survival schedule; shortened periods undercut indemnity and true-up protections that the valuation summary and creditor recoveries implicitly assume remain available through the Exhibit B windows. Schedule 5.2 retained-liability timing also assumes Exhibit B survival.
Economic / plan
effect:               Material erosion of post-effective-date protection; potential misalignment with disclosed recovery timing and with best-interests / feasibility showings if indemnity backstops expire early
Client posture
(controlling email):  WALK-AWAY. Any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue under the latest partner instruction (which revises and controls over earlier opposite ordering in the thread).
Recommendation:       REJECT in full. Do not counter on shortened core-rep survival. Require Committee Redline to conform to Exhibit B survival matrix with no reduction. Flag for partner escalation immediately if Committee insists. Do not package this point with the conceded basket conversion.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. RECONCILIATION TO VALUATION SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Baseline recoveries in the valuation summary are constructed on Debtor Plan indemnity cap, deductible basket, full Exhibit B survival, and MAE risk that includes the Schedule 3.7 regulatory path.
2. Committee Redline impacts on valuation:
   • Cap reduction (Dev. 1) — adverse; requires re-run of residual estate / indemnity-supported recovery cases before any acceptance.
   • Tipping basket (Dev. 2) — modestly adverse expected-value impact; client-authorized concession; update disclosure economics but no hold.
   • MAE regulatory carve-outs (Dev. 3) — primarily consummation / option-value risk rather than spot recovery; disclose and, if material, add sensitivity.
   • Survival shortening (Dev. 4) — adverse to back-ended indemnity value; walk-away; no valuation compromise available without Exhibit B conformity.
3. Recommendation: circulate a one-page valuation bridge to the committee and the Court-facing disclosure package only after Dev. 1 and Dev. 4 are resolved and Dev. 3 is cabined as above.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. RECONCILIATION TO DISCLOSURE STATEMENT EXCERPTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries) — controls MAE discussion; Committee carve-outs that swallow Schedule 3.7 must be rejected or expressly limited; disclosure statement risk factors must continue to describe these inquiries without being nullified by plan MAE text.
• Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities) — controls indemnity economics; silent cap cut and survival cut would shift these liabilities contrary to disclosed treatment; any accepted change requires conforming schedule and disclosure edits.
• Exhibit B (survival matrix) — controls survival; Committee limitation-period change is in direct conflict and is a walk-away under client instruction.
• General narrative in the Debtor disclosure statement yields to these scheduled exceptions; the deliverable positions above follow that hierarchy.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. CONTROLLING CLIENT INSTRUCTION (TRANSMITTAL / PARTNER EMAIL)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Latest message in the partner email thread revises analysis priorities and is the sole controlling instruction:

  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CONCEDE.
  • Survival-period reduction: WALK-AWAY.
  • Earlier messages in the same thread stated the opposite priority ordering; they are superseded and must not drive accept/reject calls.

This report’s accept/reject column implements only the latest instruction.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. ACCEPT / REJECT / COUNTER SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

| # | Deviation                         | Disposition        | Rationale (controlling sources)                                      |
|---|-----------------------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | Indemnification cap reduction     | REJECT / COUNTER   | Silent shift of Schedule 5.2 liabilities; not client-conceded        |
| 2 | Basket: deductible → tipping      | ACCEPT (concede)   | Latest partner email expressly concedes                              |
| 3 | MAE regulatory carve-outs         | REJECT / COUNTER   | Schedule 3.7 inquiries; preserve MAE for those matters               |
| 4 | Survival-period shortening        | REJECT (walk-away) | Conflicts with Exhibit B; latest partner email = walk-away           |

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VIII. OPEN ACTIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Transmit this deviation report to the engagement partner for confirmation of walk-away enforcement on Dev. 4.
2. Prepare conforming Committee response markup: accept Dev. 2 only; restore cap (or Schedule 5.2 carve-out); cabin MAE carve-outs around Schedule 3.7; restore Exhibit B survival in full.
3. Commission valuation bridge reflecting accepted Dev. 2 and holding Dev. 1 / 3 / 4 at Debtor Plan positions.
4. Update disclosure statement excerpts and schedules only after redline positions are locked.
5. Do not rely on any pre-revision email in the partner thread for negotiation authority.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IX. CONCLUSION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The Committee Redline is largely workable against the Debtor Plan if and only if (a) the tipping-basket concession is isolated and documented, (b) the silent indemnification-cap cut and MAE regulatory carve-outs are rejected or tightly countered against Schedule 5.2 and Schedule 3.7, and (c) the survival-period reduction is refused outright as a walk-away under the controlling partner instruction and Exhibit B. No other deviations in the Committee Redline rise to the same level on the current record.

Respectfully submitted for partner review.
— End of Plan Deviation Report —
